definitions.explanation: The midpoint of a period, process, or physical distance.
Used adverbially to indicate something is partial or incomplete.

examples.japanese: 8{月|がつ}{半|なか}ばに{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}く{予定|よてい}です。
examples.english: I plan to go on a trip in mid-August.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}は{半|なか}ばまで{終|お}わった。
{半|なか}ば{諦|あきら}めていたが、{最後|さいご}に{成功|せいこう}した。
examples.english: I had half given up, but I succeeded in the end.

notes:
USAGE: {半|なか}ば can function as both a noun (midpoint) and an adverb (partially, half).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・〜{月|がつ}{半|なか}ば (mid-month)
・{年|ねん}{半|なか}ば (mid-year)
・{半|なか}ば{過|す}ぎ (past the halfway point)
・{半|なか}ば{諦|あきら}める (half give up)
・{半|なか}ば{強制的|きょうせいてき}に (semi-forcibly)
・{道|みち}の{半|なか}ば (halfway along the road)

NUANCE: When used adverbially with verbs or adjectives, {半|なか}ば suggests the action or state is incomplete or partial. It often carries a nuance of ambivalence.
